economy.summary: Mulvey lists strengthening local businesses among her campaign priorities, and her campaign site says she will fight for better jobs in the district.
economy.short: Strengthen local businesses; fight for better jobs.

taxes.summary: Mulvey lists lower taxes among her stated campaign priorities.
taxes.short: Lists lower taxes among her campaign priorities.

education.summary: Mulvey lists supporting public education among her campaign priorities.
education.short: Lists supporting public education among her priorities.

healthcare.summary: Mulvey, a registered nurse and school nurse, lists protecting rural healthcare among her campaign priorities; her campaign site says she will fight for affordable access to quality, local healthcare.
healthcare.short: Protect rural healthcare; fight for affordable local healthcare access.

economy.summary: Says he plans to support small businesses. Says he is running because Farrell and Sharon are overlooked and the area lacks leadership in Harrisburg.
economy.short: Plans to support small businesses; says Farrell and Sharon are overlooked.

education.summary: Says he plans to look at improving the public school system. He has served three years on the Sharon City School Board.
education.short: Plans to look at improving the public school system.

guns.summary: Lists community safety and criminal reform among the priorities he plans to pursue, along with strengthening senior services. He has not made a specific statement on firearms.
guns.short: Lists community safety and criminal reform among his priorities.

economy.summary: Says an economy that works only for the cities is not working for his district; wants to reinvest in skilled trades and vocational education and attract employers who hire locally. Supports giving families and current residents the opportunity to buy a home before corporate investors do, and taxing corporate-owned housing.
economy.short: Reinvest in skilled trades; let residents buy homes before investors.

taxes.summary: Calls for full elimination of school property taxes, replaced by a consumption tax with a credit for essentials, paired with pension reform. Says Harrisburg has a spending problem rather than a revenue problem, and points to his township's record of not levying a property tax.
taxes.short: Eliminate school property taxes; replace with consumption tax; restrain spending.

education.summary: Wants to reinvest in skilled trades and vocational education as alternatives to four-year degrees. Notes that roughly 44 cents of every dollar funding public schools comes from local property taxes, a funding structure he wants to replace.
education.short: Reinvest in vocational education and skilled trades as degree alternatives.

healthcare.summary: Supports expanding the roles of nurse practitioners and physician assistants in underserved areas and treats telehealth and broadband as essential healthcare infrastructure. Proposes tax credits, state certification reimbursement, and school credit for training to support volunteer fire and EMS crews.
healthcare.short: Expand nurse practitioner roles; treat telehealth as essential infrastructure.

guns.summary: Says he will make sure local police, fire, and EMS have the backing, training, and resources to do the job, and will defend the constitutional rights of Carbon County residents against efforts in Harrisburg to chip away at them, stating that safety and liberty are not opposites.
guns.short: Back police, fire, EMS; defend residents' constitutional rights.

economy.summary: Said he entered the race to improve what he sees as "failed policies" that result in seniors and others losing their homes and in rising prices of utilities and gas. Stated his campaign focus as "Affordability, Accountability, Improvement, and Reform."
economy.short: Says failed policies raise utility, gas prices; focus on affordability, reform.

guns.summary: Cited public safety concerns among his reasons for running. No specific proposals on guns or public safety have been reported.
guns.short: Cited public safety concerns as a reason for running.

economy.summary: Says she wants to help families achieve financial security for peace of mind and to be able to leave something for the next generation at home in Pennsylvania.
economy.short: Help families achieve financial security and peace of mind.

taxes.summary: Calls for fiscal discipline focused on priorities so the state spends only what it has. Cites her record as a school board member of voting against tax increases 13 years in a row.
taxes.short: Spend only what state has; voted against tax increases.

education.summary: Supports accountability, investment, and innovation in schools to prepare students to succeed, and wants to increase parental involvement. Says she would request a seat on the House Education Committee, citing 14 years as a North Allegheny school director.
education.short: Supports school accountability, investment, innovation; increase parental involvement.

healthcare.summary: Says she wants to reduce healthcare costs and increase accessibility to quality care.
healthcare.short: Reduce healthcare costs and increase accessibility to quality care.

guns.summary: Says she will support police and emergency responders and bring residents and law enforcement together to meet shared goals. Has not stated a position specific to firearms policy.
guns.short: Support police and emergency responders; bring residents and police together.

economy.summary: In her 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Ward said she would promote policies that stimulate growth and create opportunities for all residents, and would attract businesses and jobs by streamlining the regulatory process and cutting red tape.
economy.short: Promote growth, attract jobs by streamlining regulation, cutting red tape.

taxes.summary: Ward said she would lower taxes and inflation by reallocating taxpayer dollars to effective programs and reducing unnecessary spending. She also said financial transparency about how government spends taxpayer money is crucial and advocates open financial reporting.
taxes.short: Lower taxes by reducing unnecessary spending; advocate open financial reporting.

education.summary: Ward, an East Pennsboro Area School District board director, said she would prioritize strong reading programs, advocate for better resources and support for teachers, and emphasize hands-on learning in the curriculum.
education.short: Prioritize reading programs, support teachers, emphasize hands-on learning.

healthcare.summary: Ward identified ensuring access to affordable healthcare, especially in rural areas, as a pressing state challenge and said Pennsylvania needs solutions to expand access and improve quality of care for an aging population facing rising costs.
healthcare.short: Expand affordable healthcare access and improve care, especially rural areas.

energy.summary: Ward said Pennsylvania must develop strategies to address environmental challenges while balancing economic growth, and that transitioning to clean energy sources and investing in green technologies can create jobs and promote a sustainable future.
energy.short: Address environmental challenges balancing growth; transition to clean energy.

economy.summary: Says he is committed to fostering a thriving economy with more jobs and opportunities for Pennsylvanians by reducing taxes and regulations to help businesses grow.
economy.short: Commits to fostering jobs by reducing taxes and regulations.

taxes.summary: Calls for a balanced state budget and spending taxpayer dollars wisely, focusing on cutting wasteful spending and prioritizing essential services.
taxes.short: Calls for balanced budget, cutting wasteful spending, prioritizing essential services.

education.summary: Advocates for empowering parents to make decisions about their children's education and for improving education funding and accountability to ensure a quality education for all students.
education.short: Advocates empowering parents, improving education funding and accountability.

healthcare.summary: Says he aims to improve access to affordable care without unnecessary government overreach, backing patient-centered healthcare reforms. In a May 2026 statement he said he would fight for better health care resources.
healthcare.short: Aims to improve affordable care access, backs patient-centered reforms.

energy.summary: Says he will promote Pennsylvania's energy independence through responsible resource development, balancing economic growth with environmental stewardship to safeguard natural resources.
energy.short: Promotes energy independence, balancing growth with environmental stewardship.

guns.summary: Says he is dedicated to public safety, supporting law enforcement officers and implementing policies that reduce crime and protect families.
guns.short: Supports law enforcement, backs policies reducing crime, protecting families.

economy.summary: Krawchuk says the cost of government in Pennsylvania has risen faster than inflation for decades and proposes fewer regulations so small businesses can thrive, with lower taxes leaving more money in residents' pockets.
economy.short: Proposes fewer regulations on small businesses and lower taxes.

taxes.summary: Krawchuk proposes eliminating the Pennsylvania personal income tax over four years through spending cuts, pledges to veto every tax increase, and supports requiring voter referendums for tax increases.
taxes.short: Proposes eliminating state income tax; pledges to veto tax increases.

taxes.summary: He targets about $3.5 billion in spending cuts via line-item vetoes, including subsidies for horse racing, stadiums, films, and coal, and proposes consolidating the cabinet from 24 to 8 positions.
taxes.short: Proposes $3.5 billion in line-item spending cuts and cabinet consolidation.

taxes.summary: He proposes eliminating school property taxes entirely, funded by moving students to a private-school system paid from existing state funding.
taxes.short: Proposes eliminating school property taxes through school privatization plan.

abortion.summary: Krawchuk proposes a "pro-option" framework in which a woman who does not want her pregnancy could legally abandon parental rights so others may adopt prenatally, with options including carrying to term at adopters' expense or early delivery; abortion would remain available if no one steps forward. He describes the approach as voluntary, not government coercion.
abortion.short: Proposes voluntary prenatal-adoption framework; abortion remains available otherwise.

education.summary: Krawchuk proposes privatizing Pennsylvania's public schools, giving every student an approximately $11,500 Education Savings Account funded from existing state money so parents can choose any school, selling public school buildings to private operators, and eliminating school property taxes. A new Scholastic Standards Board would set curriculum standards and testing.
education.short: Proposes privatizing public schools with $11,500 education savings accounts.

energy.summary: Krawchuk proposes treating pollution as trespass, holding polluters directly liable for cleanup rather than relying on regulation, and says the fracking boom is good for Pennsylvania, supporting it without new taxes while holding operators liable for waste violations.
energy.short: Supports fracking untaxed; proposes treating pollution as liable trespass.

energy.summary: He proposes eliminating government-granted utility monopolies and deregulating energy so consumers can choose among providers, including green power options.
energy.short: Proposes deregulating utilities so consumers choose providers, including green power.

guns.summary: Krawchuk opposes gun control, citing the Pennsylvania Constitution's right to bear arms and arguing that armed citizens deter crime; he commits to defending the right to keep and bear arms and opposes additional restrictions.
guns.short: Opposes gun control; commits to defending right to bear arms.

guns.summary: On public safety, he proposes eliminating parole for violent offenders so they serve full sentences, and ending civil asset forfeiture without a criminal conviction, which he calls "legalized theft."
guns.short: Proposes ending parole for violent offenders and conviction-less asset forfeiture.

economy.summary: Says government money printing drives up prices and makes it harder for families across the Commonwealth to plan for their future; names sound money as a central campaign issue.
economy.short: Says money printing drives up prices; backs sound money.

economy.summary: Criticized regulations he says make housing more expensive amid an affordability crisis, and pointed to his Habitat for Humanity board work putting people into homes.
economy.short: Says regulations make housing more expensive; cites Habitat work.

taxes.summary: As part of the Krawchuk-Thomas ticket, says the campaign will focus on eliminating Pennsylvania's property tax and opposing tax increases and government waste.
taxes.short: Ticket campaigns to eliminate property tax, oppose tax increases.

taxes.summary: Cites Ross Perot's balanced-budget movement as a model for forcing politicians to take sound financial management seriously.
taxes.short: Cites Perot balanced-budget movement as fiscal management model.

abortion.summary: In the Pittsburgh City Paper's 2024 U.S. Senate election guide, Thomas identified as pro-life and criticized voters who supported Roe v. Wade while not opposing vaccine mandates.
abortion.short: Identifies as pro-life; criticized Roe supporters over vaccine mandates.

education.summary: Says he will campaign alongside gubernatorial running mate Ken Krawchuk on what he calls a great plan to grow school choice throughout the Commonwealth.
education.short: Backs Krawchuk plan to grow school choice statewide.

education.summary: In his 2023 school board race he ran on offering alternatives to public schools; he has worked across public, private, and charter school settings for two decades.
education.short: Ran on offering alternatives to public schools.

healthcare.summary: His 2024 U.S. Senate platform opposed puberty blockers for minors, stating that children's capacity to provide informed consent is limited, and called for privatizing regulatory agencies.
healthcare.short: Opposed puberty blockers for minors; privatize regulatory agencies.

guns.summary: Advocates releasing people incarcerated for victimless crimes, citing U.S. incarceration rates, and notes the lieutenant governor's role as chair of Pennsylvania's Board of Pardons.
guns.short: Advocates releasing people incarcerated for victimless crimes via pardons.

economy.summary: In her nomination statement, Scott said neighbors across the district, from Ridley to Upper Darby, cannot make ends meet because of the high costs they are facing, and said change is needed.
economy.short: Says neighbors can't make ends meet because of high costs.

taxes.summary: Scott said Delaware County residents are struggling with crushing taxes, citing the county government raising taxes 47 percent, and said it is clear that change is needed.
taxes.short: Says residents struggle with crushing taxes; cites 47% county increase.

education.summary: In her nomination statement, Scott said the people of Delaware County are struggling with failing schools. She has not detailed specific education proposals.
education.short: Says people of Delaware County are struggling with failing schools.

healthcare.summary: In her nomination statement, Scott said the people of Delaware County are struggling with a broken healthcare system. She has not detailed specific healthcare proposals.
healthcare.short: Says people are struggling with a broken healthcare system.

energy.summary: Scott cited increased electricity costs coming from the state government as part of the high costs residents face, and said it is clear that change is needed.
energy.short: Cites increased electricity costs from state government; says change needed.

guns.summary: In her nomination statement, Scott said the people of Delaware County are struggling with unsafe streets. She has not stated positions on firearms policy.
guns.short: Says people of Delaware County are struggling with unsafe streets.
